sketches.title: Tiny Titans
sketches.premise: You and your rival command tiny creatures and objects in a chain of sudden victories. On your turn, name one small thing that defeats the thing currently standing, then explain the plain action that makes it win.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new thing directly defeats, blocks, traps, eats, or changes the standing thing; dodging, merely surviving, using a bigger copy, or naming a close cousin from the same family loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I play [thing]: [clear action against the standing thing]." Example: "I play spider: it traps the fly in its web." The host declares: "The fly has met a net with eight-legged paperwork!"

sketches.title: Bug-Trap Builders
sketches.premise: You are rival inventors building one tiny trap at a time. Each move must add a small, standing part that defeats the current part by catching it, jamming it, cutting its power, or making it harmless; the chain ends when a part cannot do that.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks for a new trap part that acts directly on the standing part; hiding from it, enduring it, adding a larger version, or swapping in a near-identical part does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I add [part], which [direct action]." Example: "I add glue, which jams the flywheel by sticking its edge." The host announces: "The flywheel has been promoted to furniture!"

sketches.title: The Crumb Court
sketches.premise: A royal crumb court settles tiny disputes by sending one small creature or object to overrule the last claimant. Your new courtier must plainly capture, consume, block, or undo what stands, and the monarch is not impressed by mere escape.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new claimant directly defeats the standing claimant; surviving, running away, growing larger, or choosing another member of the same kind is ruled a loss.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I summon [small thing], and it [specific action]." Example: "I summon an ant, and it carries away the crumb." The host proclaims: "The crumb has been sentenced to community service!"
sketches.first_card: A sugar cube declaring itself king.

sketches.title: Backyard Battles
sketches.premise: Turn a backyard scene into a ladder of clever counters. Each turn names one insect or small backyard thing that acts on the current one and defeats it in an ordinary, easy-to-picture way.
sketches.criterion: The Judge accepts only a direct defeat such as eating, trapping, crushing, poisoning, freezing, or stopping; dodging, merely being tougher, a bigger version, and a related creature with the same weakness all fail.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I am [thing], and I [action] to [standing thing]." Example: "I am a ladybug, and I eat the aphids on the leaf." The host cries: "The aphids have been evicted by a spotted landlord!"

sketches.title: Pocket-Scale Showdown
sketches.premise: Everything must be small enough to fit in a pocket, sit on a desk, or be spotted in a garden. Players alternate naming a thing whose simple use or nature defeats the thing before it, creating a brisk chain of tiny triumphs.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new thing acts on and overcomes the standing thing by stopping, trapping, breaking, soaking, burning, eating, or transforming it; dodging, surviving, bigger copies, and family cousins are not victories.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "My pocket champion is [thing]; it [action] against [standing thing]." Example: "My pocket champion is a magnet; it pulls the metal pin away from the compass needle." The host hisses: "The pin has been magnetically reassigned!"

sketches.title: Microscopic Mayhem
sketches.premise: Play a chain of tiny natural forces, creatures, and everyday objects, each one plainly overcoming the last. The smaller the scene, the bigger the drama: a seed, drop, bug, grain, or speck may rule the round if its action truly wins.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks for a direct mechanism that defeats, blocks, consumes, dissolves, dries, sticks, or changes the standing thing; evasion, endurance, a larger copy, and a merely related form are rejected.
sketches.move_shape: Say: "I become [small thing], doing [mechanism] to [standing thing]." Example: "I become a sponge, soaking up the drop of water." The host declares: "The drop has been promoted from puddle-maker to sponge's lunch!"
sketches.first_card: A drop of water balanced on a leaf.
